result.title: Toward User-Centered Agentic Recommendation: When Does Platform Competition Benefit Users?
result.summary: Conventional recommender systems operate within platform-specific catalogs, limiting access to potentially valuable resources across platforms. We propose user-centered agentic recommendation, a paradigm in which user agents compare recommendations from competing platform agents, and formalize their interaction as a repeated game. Platforms strategically modify descriptions without changing intrinsic item value, while each user agent assesses platform credibility using feedback from consumed items only. Our analysis shows that expanded resource access need not improve user welfare: strategic misrepresentation and limited verification can offset the benefits of platform competition. We quantify when platform credibility assessment allows users to benefit from broader access despite strategic exaggeration. Our analysis identifies resource and reporting conditions that guarantee higher average welfare than the original platform with an interaction budget linear in platform count. Experiments on synthetic and Amazon-grounded markets show that credibility assessment can improve finite-horizon utility, while its benefits depend on market size and mechanism parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「以用户为中心的 agentic 推荐」：用户 agent 比较多个竞争平台 agent 的推荐，并将交互形式化为重复博弈；平台可在不改变物品真实价值的前提下策略性改写描述，用户仅依据已消费物品的反馈评估平台可信度。论文分析在何种资源与报告条件下，更广的跨平台访问能真正提升用户平均福利，并用合成市场与 Amazon 数据实验检验有限时域效用。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「有限验证预算下的可信度评估与策略性误报」框架可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、验证成本与停止决策的问题表述提供借鉴。
